title: Eventual equality of descended quasi-compact opens
statement: Fix the nonempty directed preorder $I$, inverse system $D:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sch}$ with affine transitions, limit cone $c$ with vertex $S$, base index $i_0$, morphism $p:Y_0\to D(i_0)$ with $Y_0$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and quasi-compact opens $W_1,W_2\subseteq Y_0$ whose inverse images in $Y_0\times_{D(i_0)}S$ agree, as in [def-nagata-qc-open-equality-stage]. Fix the selected binary upper bounds $d$ with $i\le d(i,j)$ and $j\le d(i,j)$ and auxiliary linear order $r$ of [def-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound]. Let $\sigma=\lambda_{W_1=W_2}$ be exactly the stage returned by [def-nagata-qc-open-equality-stage] with these data. For every $j\ge i_0$ satisfying $\sigma\le j$, the inverse images of $W_1$ and $W_2$ under the first projection $Y_0\times_{D(i_0)}D(j)\to Y_0$ agree. Here the map $D(j)\to D(i_0)$ is the transition corresponding to $i_0\le j$, so these are precisely the opens on the base-changed system [def-nagata-basechanged-system]. The condition $j\ge i_0$ only specifies its indexing tail: the upper-bound property implies $i_0\le\sigma$, hence it excludes no stage above $\sigma$.

proof.text: Unfold the selected stage of [def-nagata-qc-open-equality-stage]. Its chosen compact-open equality witness in the base-changed limit system has underlying index τ, and its equality is equality of inverse images under the first projection to Y₀. By [lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound], both i₀ and τ are below the selected finite upper bound σ, using the upper-bound property of d. For j≥σ, transitivity gives τ≤j. Pull the witness equality back along the base-changed transition map from j to τ supplied by [def-nagata-basechanged-system]. Its compatibility with the first projections, and functoriality of inverse images, give equality of the two opens at j.

statement_change.old_statement: Fix the base-changed inverse system, opens, affine charts, finite basic-open presentations, transported sections, witness identities, and selected stage $\lambda_{W_1=W_2}$ constructed in [def-nagata-qc-open-equality-stage]. For every index $\lambda\geq\lambda_{W_1=W_2}$, let $W_{i,\lambda}$ be the pullback of $W_{i,\lambda_0}$ to $Y_\lambda$ (equivalently, the finite union of the transported basic opens on each chart). Then $W_{1,\lambda}=W_{2,\lambda}$ as opens of $Y_\lambda$.
statement_change.what: The landed equality-stage definition was corrected to choose a geometric equality witness rather than chartwise power-identity data. Remove references to those nonexistent outputs, retain its full geometric inputs and the same selected stage, and prove equality at every later stage from equality on the limit. The first worker instead assumed equality at an arbitrary selected stage, which removed the main obligation and did not support the citers. This repair restores that obligation. The upper-bound property of d is explicit, as required by its recorded definition. No unit statement changes.

old_proof.text: The definition node supplies a finite affine cover and, on each chart, power identities witnessing both radical containments. Every element of the finite set $F$ of the definition is $\leq\lambda_{W_1=W_2}=u(F)\leq\lambda$ by [lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound], so $\lambda$ is above every element of $F$ and, applying the transition ring maps, every identity transports to the $\lambda$-chart with the pullbacks $f_{ijk,\lambda}$. If a point lies in $D(f_{1jk,\lambda})$, the first identity forces at least one $f_{2\ell k,\lambda}$ to be nonzero at that point, so $D(f_{1jk,\lambda})\subseteq\bigcup_\ell D(f_{2\ell k,\lambda})$; the second identity gives the reverse inclusion after exchanging $1$ and $2$. Taking the finite unions and then the affine charts gives $W_{1,\lambda}\subseteq W_{2,\lambda}$ and $W_{2,\lambda}\subseteq W_{1,\lambda}$, hence equality.
